parsed.title: Behind the CAPTCHA: ClickFix, WallStealer and a Hidden Miner
parsed.summary: The report examines an open directory identified during a July 2026 investigation that hosted a fake Cloudflare verification script and several protected executables. The lure is a ClickFix-style page that tricks users into pasting an obfuscated PowerShell command into Windows Run to download and launch an executable. The executables are Rust droppers that deliver WallStealer, a credential and data stealer targeting browsers, Telegram, Discord, Steam, FileZilla and wallet data. The stealers use Steam profile pages as a dead-drop resolver to find command-and-control destinations, which is the key signal for defenders. A separate loader delivers an XMRig-based Monero miner, and defenders should watch for pasted PowerShell, temporary executable creation, unusual Steam-profile requests and files in C:\ProgramData\NVDisplay.

parsed.title: RUSTGate: A Drone-Swarm Lure Points to Potential Defence-Sector Targeting
parsed.summary: RUSTGate is an unsigned Rust-based remote-access trojan, identifying itself as RUSTGate Client v2.0, delivered through a PDF-themed shortcut that launches a batch downloader from a staging server. The lure uses a drone-swarm research decoy, suggesting potential targeting of defence-sector or unmanned-systems personnel, though the researchers did not confirm a victim or attribution. The implant executes arbitrary shell commands, transfers files in both directions, and automatically collects documents, archives, images and configuration files from all logical drives. It persists through a scheduled task named NetworkDiagnostics and communicates with its controller over plain HTTP using AES-256-GCM with a hardcoded key. A bounded probe found the controller live and accepting registrations but returning no commands. Defenders should hunt for the full delivery chain, including rundll32 launching a minimised shell and batch files written to C:\Windows\Temp, and preserve upload_state.json on suspected hosts.
